texts.facts: 3. The prosecution case is that on 20.10.1999 at about 7.30 a.m. the complainant / Food Inspector went to an illegal vendor Mansoor Ali having his shop near the Parcel Office Road at the Railway Station and found 20 litres of milk stored for preparing tea. He showed his intention to the illegal Mansoor Ali vs State Of U.P. on 27 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120342854/ 1 vendor to collect sample of it and prepared Form-6 by introducing himself. The vendor and his witnesses signed on it. He then took 750 milliliter milk kept in a vessel at the shop and paid Rs. 7.50 for it for being sent for analysis. He gave a receipt for the said purchase which was signed by the vendor and his witnesses. The purchased milk was then kept in three bottles equally in which the required formalin was added and they were sealed. The required formalities thereafter were done and one of the bottles was then sent to the public analyst, Lucknow for analysis who vide his report dated 17.11.1999 opined that milk fat was deficient by about 71 percent and milk solids non fat was deficient by about 11 percent. The sample was thus found to be adulterated. The report of the public analyst is Exb:Ka-9 to the records. A complaint was filed after obtaining sanction of the necessary formalities. The accused denied the prosecution case. The trial court convicted the revisionist as stated above.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned counsel for the revisionist raised two submissions which are as follows:- (i) Admittedly, the sample of milk was taken was from a tea shop of the revisionist which as per the complainant himself was kept for preparation of tea. The law on the subject is crisp and trite as has been held in the cases of Jagdish Singh and another vs. State of U.P.: 1998 (36) ACC 591 and B.K. Chaudhary and others vs. State of U.P. & others: Crl. Misc. (482) Application No. 5601 of 2009 decided on 15.07.2010. 7.
